name: Tally
tagline: Notion-like form builder with generous free tier and paid branding/features

pricing.notes: Official pricing/help checked 2026-07-30; Tally Pro listed at $29/month or $290/year, while pricing page also displayed a promo annual-effective $24/month.
pricing.freeTier: The free plan covers unlimited forms and submissions under fair use.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited forms/submissions/e-signatures; 10 MB/file. Fair-use examples: 50,000 submissions/month, 100 GB uploads/month, 500 GB total storage or 50,000 emails/month.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited team members, unlimited forms/submissions under fair use and 30-day version history; removes the 10 MB upload cap.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited team members, unlimited forms/submissions under fair use and 90-day version history.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited forms, submissions and e-signatures; 10 MB/file. Fair-use review examples begin with 50,000 submissions/month, 100 GB of uploads/month, 500 GB total storage or 50,000 email notifications/month.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (2 months free, about 17%); annual paid upfront and auto-renews; no paid-plan trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: Consistent use around 50,000 submissions/month, 100 GB uploads/month, 500 GB total storage or 50,000 emails/month can trigger a custom plan billed quarterly on top of the existing subscription.

verdictSummary: A form builder that stores responses and sends webhooks/email is a classic one-sitting/weekend app.
coreLoopDIY: Create form schema/editor, render public forms, store responses, export CSV, and send webhook/email notifications.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for low-friction forms, branding removal, and integrations.

priorArt.name: Formbricks
priorArt.desc: Open-source form/survey platform useful for response collection and feedback workflows.

alternatives.name: OpnForm
alternatives.desc: Open-source forms with unlimited respondents; the free self-hosted builder team stops at two

alternatives.name: HeyForm
alternatives.desc: Tally's conversational cousin, minus the document-like editor

rejectedAlternatives.name: Baserow
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Standard forms are free; one-question Survey Mode is paid, and the editor is database-first

notes: One of the cleanest yes products; enough prior art to be actionable.
prompt:
Build me a personal form builder to replace Tally. Requirements:

- One Node + Express + better-sqlite3 app, server-rendered pages, deployed on my VPS
  behind Caddy. No frontend framework.
- Admin UI at /admin, protected by a single ADMIN_TOKEN from .env, no user accounts:
  create a form, add fields (text, textarea, email, select, checkbox, file upload),
  mark required, reorder.
- Each form gets a public page at /f/<slug>: single column, one accent color, client
  and server validation, honeypot field plus a per-IP rate limit for spam.
- Responses stored in SQLite; file uploads go to uploads/<form-slug>/, 10 MB cap.
- Per form, two optional notifications: email me each response via SMTP creds in
  .env, and POST the response JSON to a webhook URL.
- Admin response view: sortable table per form with a CSV export button.
- No telemetry, no third-party form service; respondent data stays in my SQLite file.
- Out of scope: partial submissions, conditional logic, payments, and team
  workspaces. Do not build a template gallery.
- README: .env vars, Caddy snippet, where uploads and the DB live on disk.
